newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Evergreen buys properties for NZ$10.7 mln.
newsitem.headline: Evergreen buys properties for NZ$10.7 mln.

text.p: Evergreen Forests Ltd said on Tuesday that it would pay NZ$10.7 million for two freehold properties.
The purchases of land and trees were in Northland and Gisborne. The properties, Te Kuri and Te Marunga, comprise 2,846 hectares and include 1,341 stocked hectares.
The purchases are conditional upon Overseas Investment Commission consent.
Te Kuri has been purchased from Landcorp. Te Marunga was privately owned. The consideration for Te Marunga includes 323,077 shares issued at NZ$0.65.
Chief Executive Mark Bogle said the properties represented good value and met the company's objective of acquiring quality forests which complement existing holdings.
The planted area, established between 1972 and 1991, would increase Evergreen's forest holdings by more than 10 percent.
"We have existing properties in close proximity to both Te Kuri and Te Marunga so there will be operational synergies," he said.
By the end of 1997 Evergreen intended to have a fully planted contiguous 6,000 hectare forest on the Pouto Peninsula and a grouping of similar size on the East Coast.
"As outlined in our last annual report, our priority is to pursue new acquisitions in what for us is a favourable investment climate," he said.
